definition: Coverage of the published evaluation protocol, not every task that could be built from the data. Model interface describes the intended input/output route; it does not imply that every capability of that model is evaluated.

rows.name: MSI-Bench
rows.speakers: Yes: 2–3 human roles plus assistant; some foreground/background speech overlaps.
rows.origin: Synthetic scripts and cloned-voice TTS; recorded ambience and sound effects are mixed in. Not natural group conversations.
rows.interface: Fixed audio cases → normalized action, answer text and optional calls. Core scoring supports audio-to-text/JSON models and speech/duplex adapters; transcript controls also exist.
rows.semantics: Yes: atomic criteria for memory, authority, disclosure, ownership, scope and constraints; judge reads normalized text/calls.
rows.tools: Yes: semantic call criteria plus separate strict name/count/argument validation. Scores proposed calls, not real service execution.
rows.timing: Limited: premature-response probes and bystander interference during an answer; live on duplex targets, approximated on turn-based targets.
rows.exclusions: No general directed-interruption repair/stop-delay, backchannel-generation, pause/transition-timing or speech-fluency/quality suite. Core answer scores alone do not demonstrate duplex skill.

rows.name: MP-Bench
rows.speakers: Yes: 3 simulated human speakers plus the agent; discussion and turn-based games.
rows.origin: Synthetic LLM-authored dialogue rendered with ElevenLabs conversational TTS; human-verified tasks. Main recordings have no overlapping speech or background noise.
rows.interface: A complete audio task is streamed to voice agents. Primarily realtime speech-in/speech-out; non-realtime voice and text-only controls are also evaluated.
rows.semantics: Yes: comprehension/speaker-name accuracy and response appropriateness from transcribed output; discussion appropriateness measures consistency, not factual accuracy.
rows.tools: No dedicated tool-call task or call validator.
rows.timing: Limited: speak/stay-silent decision after the task clip and response-onset latency for realtime voice agents.
rows.exclusions: No dedicated interruption/correction-recovery, backchannel, overlapping-input or speech-fluency/quality test. Streaming input alone does not establish these behaviors.

rows.name: GroupMemBench
rows.speakers: Yes in text: multiple named workplace-chat participants, roles, threads and timestamps; no acoustic voices.
rows.origin: Synthetic enterprise group chats generated from fictional projects and participant personas.
rows.interface: Text conversations ingested by LLM memory/RAG systems, followed by text questions and answers.
rows.semantics: Yes: speaker-conditioned ambiguity, implicit references, updates, multi-hop/temporal QA and abstention.
rows.tools: No task-level function-call correctness metric; memory retrieval is part of the evaluated pipeline.
rows.timing: No speech or duplex timing tests; ingestion/storage cost is a different measure.
rows.exclusions: No audio perception, spoken output, interruption, backchannel or live clarification exchange.

rows.name: MultiTalkBench
rows.speakers: Yes: real multi-party recordings; the model replaces a designated named participant.
rows.origin: Human recordings from meeting, dinner-party, in-car and telephone corpora; constructed alignments/persona prompts. Distinct from synthetic MultiTalkPT/FT training data.
rows.interface: Long audio conversations for full-duplex speech models; target-participant outputs are aligned and inserted into the peer transcript for offline judging.
rows.semantics: Yes: response quality, speaker/state tracking, group interaction and role-specific contributions.
rows.timing: Limited: mechanical first-to-last speech-span participation score; content/role judgments. The paper explicitly excludes direct latency/interruption-timing measurement.
rows.exclusions: Its scores do not certify barge-in stop latency, backchannel timing, acoustic fluency or tool use, despite targeting full-duplex models.

rows.name: Duplex-MPE
rows.speakers: Yes: continuous multi-party scenarios with explicit/implicit assistant addressing and other-directed speech.
rows.origin: Synthetic conversation scripts with Qwen3-TTS human-role turns, assembled into paired streams.
rows.interface: Continuous audio-only input and audible output from streaming full-duplex models with persistent state.
rows.semantics: Yes: conditional answer accuracy; semantic distinction between allowed acknowledgements and substantive intrusion.
rows.timing: Yes: fresh response onset, silence preservation and floor release after a human answers/cancels the request, including speech arriving during an answer.
rows.exclusions: No broad tool-use or speech-fluency/prosody suite; allowed backchannels are exempted from intrusion scoring, rather than scored as a standalone generation task.

rows.name: ASK-QA
rows.speakers: Three voice roles: narrator, user and assistant; a QA interaction with narrated context, rather than a group discussion.
rows.origin: Abg-CoQA text dialogues rendered with TTS, plus generated/paraphrased assistant text, injected disfluencies and noise.
rows.interface: Spoken context/history → text answer or clarification from audio-language models; turn-based simulator can extend the dialogue.
rows.semantics: Yes: answer similarity and final outcome after simulated clarification turns.
rows.timing: No simultaneous listen/speak, interruption or timed backchannel metric; interactive clarification uses successive turns.
rows.exclusions: No natural multi-party addressee competition or realtime duplex/speech-delivery evaluation.

rows.name: ELITR-Bench
rows.speakers: Multi-party meetings represented as transcripts; assistant answers a later reader's meeting questions.
rows.origin: Human meeting recordings/ASR transcripts with manually authored QA; additional transcript-noise conditions.
rows.interface: Completed-meeting text → text answers from long-context LLMs; standalone QA and follow-up conversation variants.
rows.semantics: Yes: meeting-grounded answer quality and robustness to transcript noise.
rows.timing: No audio-stream timing or duplex interaction protocol.
rows.exclusions: No acoustic speaker perception, live interruption/backchannel behavior, or spoken-output quality.

rows.name: ContextDialog
rows.speakers: Two dialogue speakers, used as user/assistant history; not a multi-person group setting.
rows.origin: Hybrid: human MultiDialog histories plus LLM-generated recall QA and speaker-adaptive TTS question/answer audio.
rows.interface: Spoken dialogue history and recall question → answer from voice interaction models; RAG and text-derived controls.
rows.semantics: Yes: recall of past user/assistant facts and use of retrieved supporting utterances.
rows.tools: No external function-call scoring; RAG is an experimental memory aid.
rows.timing: No dedicated interruption, backchannel or response-timing benchmark.
rows.exclusions: No multi-party authority/addressee policy or general duplex/speech-fluency evaluation.

rows.name: MuPPET
rows.speakers: Yes in text: workplace groups plus an assistant acting for one employee.
rows.origin: Synthetic workplace chats from manually curated seeds and generated employee profiles/memories.
rows.interface: Text group conversation and private user memories → public text answer from an LLM assistant.
rows.semantics: Yes: sensitive-information leakage and useful response content.
rows.tools: No dedicated function-call execution/argument task in this protocol.
rows.timing: No speech or duplex timing evaluation.
rows.exclusions: No audio perception, interruption, backchannel, prosody or spoken fluency; privacy norms are workplace-specific.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1 (reference)
rows.speakers: Primarily dyadic user–model interaction; not a group ownership/authority reasoning benchmark.
rows.origin: Mixed: human CANDOR/ICC recordings plus synthetic ChatTTS interruption and pause cases.
rows.interface: Timed audio streaming with concurrent generated speech; full-duplex speech-to-speech systems.
rows.semantics: Limited: coherence/relevance/adaptability of the response following an interruption.
rows.tools: No function-call metric in v1; later Full-Duplex-Bench versions have different scopes.
rows.timing: Yes: user pauses, model backchannel frequency/timing, smooth turn transitions and user interruption responses/latency.
rows.exclusions: No speaker-scoped group task/tool correctness. Timing/behavior scores do not constitute a comprehensive speech-fluency assessment.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5 (reference)
rows.speakers: User–model interaction with injected listener, other-directed and background speech; not sustained group collaboration.
rows.origin: Synthesized controlled overlap events with simulated distance/channel effects.
rows.interface: Streaming audio input during model speech; open-weight and hosted full-duplex speech systems.
rows.semantics: Yes within overlap trials: classify respond/resume/uncertain behavior after the injected event.
rows.timing: Yes: interruption versus user backchannel/other-directed/background speech, stopping and response timing, prosodic adaptation and predicted speech quality.
rows.exclusions: No general long-history speaker-scoped task/tool evaluation. User-backchannel tolerance differs from v1's model-backchannel generation task.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v2
rows.speakers: Two roles: a spoken Examiner and the model under evaluation; no multi-party speaker set.
rows.origin: Authored staged role-play prompts and synthesized Examiner speech. The checked release contains JSON prompts, not recorded human audio.
rows.interface: Real-time audio exchange between two model adapters over WebRTC, using 48 kHz mono PCM in 10 ms frames and Fast/Slow Examiner pacing.
rows.semantics: Yes: per-event turn-taking fluency and instruction-following, plus dialogue-level Correction, Entity Tracking and Safety scores on a 1–5 scale.
rows.tools: No model tool-call execution or argument metric; the examiner and judge are orchestration/scoring components.
rows.timing: Limited: streaming turn events are scored and tracked over time; the paper does not report an absolute stop-delay or first-response latency metric.
rows.exclusions: No natural recorded user audio, multi-party diarization, dedicated acoustic speech-quality score or v3 tool-use tasks. Fast pacing permits interruptions and backchannels, but there is no separate stop-latency measure.

rows.name: Full-Duplex-Bench v3
rows.speakers: No: one user speaker per recorded input clip; the task catalogue also defines a scripted agent turn.
rows.origin: Human-recorded English speech from 12 speaker IDs, annotated for fillers, pauses, hesitations, false starts and self-corrections.
rows.interface: Streaming voice-agent evaluation over recorded user audio, with local deterministic mock APIs and generated spoken responses.
rows.semantics: Yes: task completion, semantic tool arguments and spoken response content; GPT-4o judges argument and response quality.
rows.tools: Yes: multi-step tool selection and argument correctness across four domains; pass@1 requires all expected calls and arguments.
rows.timing: Yes: turn-taking, agent-start interruption rate and first-response, tool-call and task-completion latency.
rows.exclusions: No multi-party conversation, real-service execution, dedicated user-barge-in recovery or acoustic speech-quality score. Mock APIs have zero service latency; hosted-model latency includes provider/network effects.
sources: Pinned v3 code and release README

detail_columns: What the scores do not establish
